tex_content.html:
Theorem
[Global gradient bound in divergence form]1. ch15:15.6\group ch15-global-interior-gradient Let $u\in C^2(\Omega )$ satisfy (15.56) in the bounded domain $\Omega $, and assume (15.59), (15.60). Then

\[ \sup _{\Omega }|Du|\le C igl(1+\sup _{\partial \Omega }|Du| igr) ag {15.63} \]

where $C$ depends on $n$, $ au $, $ u (M)$, and the quantities in (15.60).
Proof

\sketch Apply Theorem 8.16 to the differentiated equations (15.57) on the region where $|Du|$ is larger than half its maximum. Estimate (15.61) and the little-$o$ condition (15.60) give (15.62), which absorbs the large-gradient term and yields (15.63).

□

For the interior estimate assume uniform ellipticity in the form

egin{equation} |D_p A(x,z,p)| \le \mu (|z|)(1+|p|)^ au ag {15.64} \end{equation}

where $\mu >0$ is nondecreasing. If $ au >-1$, then (15.59), (15.64) imply

\[ p\cdot A(x,z,p)-p\cdot A(x,z,0)\ge rac{ u }{ au +1}|p|^{ au +2}. \]

egin{equation} |A^i(x,z,p)-A^i(x,z,0)|\le rac{\mu }{ au +1}(1+|p|)^{ au +1},\qquad i=1,\dots ,n. ag {15.65} \end{equation}

Assume also

egin{equation} g(x,z,p)=(1+|p|)\, |D_z A|+|D_x A|+|B|\le \mu (|z|)(1+|p|)^{ au +2} ag {15.66} \end{equation}

on $\Omega imes \mathbb R imes \mathbb R^n$.

(i) $L^p$ reduction. Test (15.57) with $\zeta D_ku$, sum in $k$, set $v=|Du|^2$, and apply Young's inequality:

egin{equation} \int _{\Omega }\left( ilde{a}^{ij}D_j v+2D_k u\, f_k^i ight)D_i\zeta \, dx\le rac12\int _{\Omega }\zeta \lambda ^{-1}\sum (f_k^i)^2\, dx ag {15.67} \end{equation}

for nonnegative $\zeta \in C_0^1(\Omega )$. Set

\[ ar{v}=\int _0^v (1+\sqrt{t})^ au \, dt, \]

Then (15.67) becomes

egin{equation} \int _{\Omega }\left( ilde{a}^{ij}D_j ar{v}+2D_k u\, f_k^i ight)D_i\zeta \le rac12\int _{\Omega }\zeta \lambda ^{-1}\sum (f_k^i)^2\, dx, ag {15.68} \end{equation}

where

\[ ilde{a}^{ij}= ar{a}^{ij}(1+|Du|)^{- au }. \]

Theorem 8.17 and (15.66) imply, for sufficiently large $p$, egin{equation} \sup _{B_R(y)} v \le C(n, u (M),\mu (M), au ,\operatorname {diam}\Omega ,R^{-n}\int _{B_{2R}(y)} v^p\, dx). ag {15.69} \end{equation}

(ii) Hölder reduction. The weak equation is egin{equation} \mathcal{Q}(u,\varphi )=\int _{\Omega } igl(A^i(x,u,Du)D_i\varphi -B(x,u,Du)\varphi igr)\, dx=0 \qquad orall \varphi \in C_0^1(\Omega ). ag {15.70} \end{equation}

By (15.65), egin{equation} |A(x,z,p)|\le \mu _1(|z|)(1+|p|)^{ au +1} ag {15.71} \end{equation} \[ p\cdot A(x,z,p)\ge u _1(|z|)|p|^{ au +2}-\mu _1(|z|) \] for $(x,z,p)\in \Omega imes \mathbb {R} imes \mathbb {R}^n$, where $\mu _1$ and $ u _1$ are respectively positive non-decreasing and positive non-increasing functions depending on $ au ,\mu , u $ and $\sup _{\Omega }|A(x,u,0)|$.

Test (15.70) with \[ \varphi =\eta ^2[u-u(y)] \] where $\eta \in C_0^1(B_{2R}(y))$. With $\omega (R)=\sup _{B_{2R}}|u(x)-u(y)|$, choose $R$ so that $\omega (R)\le u _1 2^{- au }/(8(\mu +\mu _1))$. Then \[ \int _{\Omega } \eta ^2 |Du|^{ au +2}\, dx \leq C \int _{\Omega } igl(\eta ^2+\omega (R)(1+|Du|)^{ au }|D\eta |^2 igr)\, dx ag {15.72} \] where $C=C(\mu ,\mu _1, u _1, au )$. Testing with \[ \eta v^{( eta +1)/2}, \qquad eta >0, \] gives \[ \int _{\Omega } \eta ^2 |Du|^{2 eta + au +4}\, dx \leq C \int _{\Omega } \Bigl\{ |Du|^{2( eta +1)} igl(\eta ^2+\omega (R)(1+|Du|)^{ au }|D\eta |^2 igr) \qquad \qquad +( eta +1)^2\omega (R)(1+|Du|)^{ au }\eta ^2 v^{ eta -1}|Dv|^2 \Bigr\} \, dx. ag {15.73} \] Testing (15.67) with $\zeta =\eta ^2v^ eta $, applying Young's inequality, and taking $\omega (R)$ sufficiently small gives a cutoff estimate. With $\eta =1$ on $B_R(y)$ and $|D\eta |\le 2/R$, gives for every $p\ge 1$ egin{equation} ag {15.74} \int _{B_R(y)}(1+|Du|)^p\, dx\leq C \end{equation} where $C=C(\mu , u ,\mu _1, u _1,p, au ,R^{-1})$. Combining (15.69) and (15.74), for $B_0=B_{R_0}(y)\Subset \Omega $ and $0<\alpha <1$, egin{equation} ag {15.75} |Du(y)|\leq C \end{equation} where $C=C(n, au , u ,\mu , u _1,\mu _1,\alpha ,[u]_{\alpha ,y})$ and \[ [u]_{\alpha ,y}=\sup _{B_0} rac{|u(x)-u(y)|}{|x-y|^\alpha }. \]

(iii) Hölder estimate for weak solutions. Rewrite (15.71), (15.66) as egin{equation} ag {15.76} egin{aligned} |A(x,z,p)|& \leq a_0|p|^{m-1}+\chi ^{m-1} \ p\cdot A(x,z,p)& \geq u _0|p|^m-\chi ^m \ |B(x,z,p)|& \leq b_0|p|^m+\chi ^m \end{aligned} \end{equation}

where $m= au +2>1$ and $a_0,b_0, u _0,\chi >0$ may depend on $M=\sup _\Omega |u|$.
